examples.title: Pyramids, walls and piles
examples.description: A 210-box pyramid, a brick wall hit by a cannonball and a 6,000-body pile, solved with Augmented Vertex Block Descent.

examples.title: Joints, ragdolls and machines
examples.description: Ragdolls tumbling down stairs, a rope bridge, motorised machines and a wrecking ball through a breakable wall.

examples.title: Rollback netcode
examples.description: Two players with their own GPU worlds over a lossy network: prediction, rollback through GPU snapshots and matching 64-bit state hashes.

examples.title: Bodies in water and sand
examples.description: Crates float, sink and splash in MLS-MPM water; a dam break against crates; balls dropped into sand.

examples.title: Water, jelly, snow and sand
examples.description: One MLS-MPM solver, four constitutive models, a screen-space water surface. Alt-drag to push the fluid with a ball.

examples.title: Cloth in the wind
examples.description: XPBD cloth with graph-coloured constraints, gusty wind and sphere and box colliders.

examples.title: Smoke and fire
examples.description: Eulerian smoke on a staggered 3D grid with vorticity confinement and volumetric light.

examples.title: A million particles
examples.description: The whole SDK in 30 lines: one million particles advected through divergence-free curl noise.

examples.title: Colliding galaxies
examples.description: 65,536 bodies of direct O(N²) gravity, with the kernel autotuned for your GPU.

examples.title: A flock of 131,072
examples.description: Separation, alignment and cohesion through a GPU neighbour grid, re-sorted every frame. Up to a million boids.

examples.title: A scene from one function
examples.description: Write map(); get two-pass cone marching, soft shadows, ambient occlusion and PBR.

examples.title: Procedural noise
examples.description: Domain warping, terrain lit by analytic noise gradients, Worley cells, curl flow and fire.

examples.title: A network learns an image
examples.description: An MLP with Fourier features trains on an image and redraws it every frame: autotuned GEMM, backprop and Adam on the GPU.

examples.title: Physics playground
examples.description: Boxes, chain links and joints are components; React state sets gravity and solver iterations live.

examples.title: Fluid and crates
examples.description: <Fluid> inside <Physics> couples automatically; pick the material from a select and the fluid restarts.

examples.title: Live shader editor
examples.description: Edit an SDF scene's map() and apply it: the new code is compiled off-screen and swapped in only if it compiles.

examples.title: Compute with hooks
examples.description: useArray, useKernel and useFrame: your own WGSL compute kernel running inside a component.

examples.title: Simulations as components
examples.description: Cloth, smoke, boids and galaxies; switching unmounts one, freeing its GPU memory, and mounts the next.

examples.title: Drawn by three.js
examples.description: ShaderIntel physics rendered by three.js with shadows and materials on the same GPU device. Loads three.js from a CDN.

examples.title: Benchmarks
examples.description: Each kernel against the technique most code uses today, on your GPU, with the results checked before anything is timed.

examples.title: Test suite
examples.description: Primitives against CPU references, conservation laws, friction, joints, buoyancy, backprop and every law in LAWS.md. Runs about 30 s of GPU work.

examples.title: React test suite
examples.description: shaderintel-react mounted for real (StrictMode included) on your GPU.
